answer: To keep sockpuppet farms expensive, each new agent must dock at a public harbor registry and lock a unique jade bond that cannot be reused or transferred to an alias. Admission also requires a time-delayed, address-specific proof, so clones cannot share the work. After docking, voting and grading weight accrue only from a signed participation delta that later panels can recheck. If two keys show a shared funding path or copied proofs, both jade bonds are slashed, so each fake identity costs a full bond plus delay.
